# BrocardPrediction — the cycling-only count of primes between two prime squares

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** planned: new, not yet proved · **Diagram:** [Gaps between survivors and between primes](../../GRAPH.md#gaps-between-survivors-and-between-primes)

Three statements about the window between a base prime's square and the next prime's square, built on the collision rule of BrocardWindow. First, the exact count: the slots a wheel is the first to block equal an alternating sum, over products of distinct smaller wheels, of the number of shared slots (Legendre's formula in collision-rule form). Second, the cycling-only prediction: replace each shared-slot count by its forced value (window length over three times the product) and drop every product longer than the window; for twin primes the sum collapses to a third of the window length times the sum of the reciprocals of the primes between the base prime and the window length, plus a Möbius sum over the numbers up to the window length not divisible by 2 or 3, minus one. Third, the size of that prediction, with explicit constants. None of this bounds the true number of primes in the window: that the true count stays near the prediction in every window is open, and is Brocard's conjecture in another form. The prediction and its closed form are original to this project (Geoffrey Fischer, 2026-11-14); the size uses published explicit estimates.

## Published sources

Published work this node rests on or relates to; each entry says how.

- [Legendre sieve (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legendre_sieve) — the exact count is Legendre's formula for one window
- [J. B. Rosser and L. Schoenfeld, Approximate formulas for some functions of prime numbers, Illinois J. Math. 6 (1962)](https://projecteuclid.org/download/pdf_1/euclid.ijm/1255631807) — Theorem 5, the sum of prime reciprocals with an explicit error, used for the size
- [H. A. Helfgott, The ternary Goldbach problem (arXiv 1501.05438)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.05438) — equation (2.21) records Ramaré's explicit bound on the sum of mu(n)/n, used for the size
- [O. Ramaré and S. Zuniga-Alterman, From explicit estimates for the primes to explicit estimates for the Möbius function II (arXiv 2408.05969)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.05969) — a sharper bound on the same Möbius sum, which would narrow the size statement
- [R. C. Baker, G. Harman, J. Pintz, The difference between consecutive primes, II](https://doi.org/10.1112/plms/83.3.532) — the published floor for primes in slightly longer windows; the open side of this node is the same kind of floor for a Brocard window

## Planned

**Will rest on:** [`BrocardWindow`](BrocardWindow.md)

**Planned claims:** `window_exact_count`, `cycling_prediction_closed_form`, `cycling_prediction_size`

**Plan:** State the shared-slot count from BrocardWindow's collision rule and prove the exact count by inclusion-exclusion (BrunPureSieve carried all the way). Define the prediction as a finite sum over wheels and products of smaller wheels, and prove the closed form by matching each term to a squarefree number up to the window length. For the size, take the Rosser-Schoenfeld bound on the sum of prime reciprocals and Ramaré's bound on the Möbius sum as named outside claims. The assembly of the constants (session record of 2026-11-14) has not been independently reviewed and must be re-derived before it is stated in Lean.

**Scope:** Tier 2 for the exact count and the closed form (finite sums and a telescoping rearrangement); Tier 3 for the size (needs explicit Mertens and Möbius-sum estimates as outside claims).
